title: Game Math Part 2 · Polygons1: Centers and Boundaries

scenes.title: 찾은 위치에서 기준점 선택으로
lines: The previous lecture described a triangle position by vertex weights. Where should we place a reference marker? The answer changes with what we want to make equal.

scenes.title: 어떤 중심을 쓰고, 어떻게 나눌까요?
lines: Does a triangle have just one center, and how can we partition terrain with an inward notch?
We will observe real game tiles and terrain, then distinguish the questions answered by centroid, incenter and circumcenter.
Next we will validate polygon boundaries and convexity, and examine the limits of a triangle fan.
Finally we will partition a concave example by ear clipping and check coverage and thin triangles.

scenes.title: 이번 편과 다음 편의 범위
lines: The complete polygon chapter is split into two episodes. This one ends after choosing centers and validating boundaries. The following episode continues with triangle partitioning.

scenes.title: 타일을 놓을 때 필요한 기준
lines: In Dorfromantik, hexagonal tiles rotate and enter empty positions. Observe each tile center and outer edges together.
Placing a central marker and fitting an interior circle ask different questions.
The center of a circle through the corners answers another question. Shape can change all three answers.
Symmetric regular hexagons make centers appear coincident; an arbitrary triangle need not do so.
Connected tiles change the entire land outline. Distinguish one tile from the combined region.
We will compare a three-four-five triangle in our own defined example, without inferring the game implementation.

scenes.title: 같은 비율은 좌표의 평균입니다
lines: Mix three points with equal weights. A weight of one third per point gives their coordinate average and connects to the balance point of a uniform paper triangle. Equal distances to every side or every vertex were not imposed.

scenes.title: 세 중심이 답하는 세 질문
lines: The centroid is the average of three triangle vertices and the intersection of the medians.
The incenter is equally distant from the three sides and centers a circle tangent inside them.
The circumcenter is equally distant from the three vertices and centers a circle through them.
Coordinate average, distance to sides, and distance to vertices: decide what should be equal first.
Compare the right triangle with vertices zero-zero, four-zero and zero-three on the same diagram.
The three centers differ here. Their shared name does not make their roles interchangeable.

scenes.title: 무게중심은 무엇의 평균일까요?
lines: Add the three vertices and divide by three. Our centroid is four thirds, one.
A median joins a vertex to the opposite midpoint; the centroid lies two thirds along it from the vertex.
The other medians meet the same point. Each vertex has barycentric weight one third.
It is also the mass center of a uniform triangular lamina. Nonuniform density requires a different calculation.
For a polygon partition, weight triangle centroids by area. Averaging polygon vertices generally gives the wrong area centroid.
Collinear vertices still have a coordinate average but no nonzero-area triangular lamina. Validate the input separately.

scenes.title: 움직이는 건물의 기준점과 외곽
lines: In Tiny Glade, place a building and change its size and position. Blue marks an observed reference; choosing one reference does not replace its complete outline.
In a separate shot, rotate a building and change its height. Its outline changes even with a similar center marker. This is an observed screen reference, not a claim about internal game calculations.

scenes.title: 가운데 표시와 안전한 여유 공간
lines: In Serious Sam2, observe the walkable surface and edges while moving between paths and bridges.
A marker location and clearance from boundaries are different geometric problems.
For a defined triangular platform, the vertex average can be one marker reference.
It does not have equal distances to all sides. Circular clearance needs side distances.
Actual paths can have complex outlines. Replacing them with one triangle loses boundaries.
Our next incenter example verifies equal side distances numerically rather than claiming the game collision method.

scenes.title: 각을 반으로 나누면 왜 변에서 같은 거리일까요?
lines: Drop perpendiculars from an interior point to two sides. On the angle bisector, the two right triangles are congruent, giving equal perpendicular distances.

Join a point equally distant from all three sides to the vertices. The three small triangles share the same radius as height. Their areas, and hence the barycentric area weights from the previous lecture, are proportional to their opposite side lengths.

scenes.title: 내심과 내접원의 반지름
lines: Angle bisectors meet at the incenter. Weight each vertex by the length of its opposite side.
The opposite lengths are five, three and four, with perimeter twelve.
Divide the weighted sum by twelve to obtain one-one, at distance one from both coordinate axes.
The hypotenuse is three x plus four y minus twelve equals zero. At the incenter, its absolute residual divided by five is also one.
The inradius is twice area divided by perimeter: twice six divided by twelve equals one.
Equivalently divide area by semiperimeter. Confusing perimeter with semiperimeter produces half the correct radius.

scenes.title: 변의 중점에서 직각으로 세우는 이유
lines: We have solved equal distances to sides. Now require equal distances to vertices. A perpendicular line through the midpoint of two points consists of positions equally distant from them. This is the perpendicular bisector.

scenes.title: 외심은 삼각형 밖에 있을 수도 있습니다
lines: Intersect perpendicular bisectors of two sides to find a center equally distant from the vertices.
Midpoints two-zero and zero-one point five give intersecting bisectors at two-one point five.
Its distance from the origin is two point five, equal to the other vertex distances: the circumradius.
A right triangle places the center at the hypotenuse midpoint; an acute triangle places it inside and an obtuse triangle outside.
The obtuse triangle zero-zero, four-zero, one-one has circumcenter two-minus one, outside but still satisfying the condition.
Collinear points do not determine a unique finite circumcircle; nearly collinear inputs are numerically unstable.

scenes.title: 벽을 바꾸면 안과 밖의 경계도 바뀝니다
lines: A wall stroke creates an open arch. Red follows the observed wall boundary.
In a separate shot, erase and redraw a wall, then run a path through it. Watch both the remaining wall and empty opening: the full boundary conveys more than one center point.

scenes.title: 지형 윤곽은 점의 순서가 중요합니다
lines: In Noita, observe protrusions and inward notches while moving through irregular terrain.
A polygon records vertices in boundary order. Reordering the same points changes the shape.
A shortcut across an inward boundary can incorrectly fill a passage or empty region.
Repeated points and tiny edges can destabilize direction and area calculations.
We use visible contours to motivate valid input, without asserting a triangle mesh implementation for pixel terrain.
Our next diagram defines a simple six-vertex concave polygon and checks its ordered boundary and missing region.

scenes.title: 선을 이어서 남겨야 할 땅을 정합니다
lines: A single center cannot describe the land shape. Connect boundary points in order and close the path to distinguish retained area from empty space. We now move from choosing a center to preserving a boundary.

scenes.title: 분할 전에 경계부터 검증하기
lines: A polygon boundary closes from its last vertex to its first; store vertices in boundary order.
Our L runs through zero-zero, four-zero, four-one, one-one, one-four, zero-four.
The upper-right missing region is outside; one-one is the concave vertex.
Check finite coordinates, duplicate points, zero-length edges and zero-area input first.
For3D vertices, check coplanarity and intersections of nonadjacent edges as well.
We partition a simple polygon without holes or self-intersections. Holes require additional contours and a suitable algorithm.

scenes.title: 볼록성은 선분으로 생각하세요
lines: A convex region contains the entire segment between every two of its points; it has no inward notch.
A regular hexagon and a triangle are convex: interior point pairs stay inside when connected.
In our L, a segment from upper-left to lower-right crosses the missing upper-right region.
Its endpoints are inside but part of the segment is outside, proving concavity.
For a valid simple planar boundary, consistent turn orientation provides another check.
Do not apply a turn test blindly to a self-intersecting contour. Validate order and intersections first.

scenes.title: 높이 변화와 평면의 홈을 구분합니다
lines: Tiny Glade changes terrain height. Different heights cannot automatically be treated as one planar boundary.
In a separate Noita cave, pass through a narrow opening and move toward the right ledge. Red follows visible land versus empty space. Bridging a notch could create land outside the original shape.

scenes.title: 타일 하나와 연결된 땅은 다릅니다
lines: Adding Dorfromantik hexagons changes the land boundary. Distinguish one tile from the entire connected region.
An individual tile is convex while its union can contain inward notches.
Connecting two land positions can cross an empty tile location.
A union of convex pieces is not necessarily convex; test its complete boundary separately.
An area with holes needs inner exclusion contours in addition to the outer boundary.
We will examine whole-shape convexity and why an angle sum alone cannot distinguish it.

scenes.title: 게임이 달라도 기준점과 경계는 구분합니다
lines: A Dorfromantik tile and a Tiny Glade building need placement references. A Serious Sam screen marker helps locate a target, while a Noita terrain boundary separates open space from solid land.

Across these different purposes, one point and a complete outline carry different information. Equal center points do not make two shapes identical. Choose coordinate averaging or equal distances to sides before calculating. These observations do not identify the games’ internal implementation.

scenes.title: 다른 동굴에서도 경계와 빈 공간을 확인합니다
lines: In another Noita interval, the character passes the right ledge. A point may mark the character, but the red terrain outline and the empty gap beside it remain separate information.
A separate shot descends and returns upward. Bridging across the ledge’s notch could incorrectly fill space that was originally open.

scenes.title: 회전의 부호는 어느 쪽으로 꺾였는지입니다
lines: The segment crossing empty space showed that the L is concave. Turning along its boundary checks the same property numerically. At its notch, travel three left and then three up: the2D cross product is minus nine, the opposite turn from the other vertices.

scenes.title: 회전 부호와 각도의 합
lines: Inspect the2D cross sign of consecutive edges. With counterclockwise winding, convex vertices turn left.
The L notch turns right, mixing turn signs in this valid simple example.
Collinear triples have zero cross product. Define strict convexity or a policy allowing collinear points.
Every simple polygon has interior-angle sum n minus two times180 degrees, whether convex or concave.
Six vertices give720 degrees. A correct angle sum alone does not prove convexity.
For acos, reject zero edges and clamp its input to minus one through one. The smaller unsigned angle does not identify a reflex interior angle.

scenes.title: 경계를 정했으니 안쪽을 나눌 차례입니다
lines: We chose centers by their purpose and found the notch in an ordered boundary. A boundary defines the outside, but does not yet partition the interior. The next episode divides this L while preserving its empty region.
